meta.title: ADHD Assistant Bot
meta.subtitle: Physical chief-of-staff device for executive dysfunction

report_card.summary: The document argues that ADHD executive dysfunction cannot be solved by passive note-taking tools. It proposes a physical ADHD assistant bot that ingests workspace, calendar, and sensor inputs and then actively nudges the user toward the few tasks requiring human attention. The design centers on a proactive chief-of-staff persona powered by Hermes and Cortex, with hardware feedback to prevent laptop-tab distraction.

story.title: Executive dysfunction stalls action
story.narration: ADHD executive dysfunction makes prioritization and task initiation collapse even when the user knows what matters. The document frames this as the core failure the ADHD Assistant Bot must directly mitigate.

story.title: Passive tools capture but never push
story.narration: Granola, Notion, and Obsidian capture context, but they never nudge or push back. The system keeps absorbing data while the user drifts to low-priority work.

story.title: A physical chief of staff avoids tab distraction
story.narration: The proposal shifts to a dedicated physical device that behaves like a chief of staff. A starter persona such as Harvey Specter anchors the tone, while the bot evolves through user behavior.

story.title: Unified inputs feed the worldview
story.narration: Workspace chat (Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams), email (Gmail, Outlook), and meeting capture (Granola) feed a unified worldview. The assistant learns what matters across workstreams and calendar shifts.

story.title: Hermes and Cortex run the reasoning loop
story.narration: Hermes acts as the agent brain while Cortex supplies the reasoning layer. The system runs a GTD/GST cycle to capture, triage, and delegate tasks in a structured loop.

story.title: Proactive nudges keep the user on track
story.narration: The bot checks in every 1–2 hours with voice prompts and physical feedback. A buzzer, LCD 16x2 display, and movement sensor keep attention anchored without opening another laptop tab.

story.title: Live demo proves the chief-of-staff moment
story.narration: On stage, the bot wakes as the presenter walks out and confirms the three agenda items in real time. The system re-prioritizes displaced tasks instantly, showing the hardware brain and reasoning layer working together.

story.title: Build plan splits capture, reasoning, and output
story.narration: The team divides input capture, GTD/GST processing, and output nudges into parallel build tasks. The plan prioritizes a local, composable architecture before expanding to other neurodivergent profiles.

insights.title: Passive capture tools create a false sense of progress without action
insights.body: Granola, Notion, and Obsidian are framed as input sinks that never push users into motion. The product vision rejects passive capture in favor of proactive nudges that surface only the tasks requiring human judgment.

insights.title: A physical device reduces tab-based distraction and boosts adherence
insights.body: By moving the assistant into a single-purpose object, the system avoids the laptop-tab trap that fuels ADHD context switching. The hardware layer becomes the anchor for attention and follow-through.

insights.title: The three-item filter is the core behavior that creates trust
insights.body: The chief-of-staff persona only surfaces the three tasks needing human input, which builds confidence that the system is protecting focus rather than demanding it. This filter defines the bot’s personality more than any explicit setting.

insights.title: Measuring success by deadlines pushed can entrench avoidance loops
insights.body: The proposed metric tracks deadlines pushed per week, which can normalize deferral if not balanced by completion signals. Without guardrails, the system could reward delay rather than progress.

insights.title: Hermes and Cortex define the bottleneck for real-time reprioritization
insights.body: All calendar shifts and task triage depend on the Hermes agent brain and the Cortex reasoning layer staying responsive. If either lags, the promise of live reprioritization collapses.

nodes.description: The compounding failure to prioritize and initiate tasks despite knowing what matters, causing drift toward low-priority work.

nodes.label: ADHD Assistant Bot
nodes.description: A dedicated physical chief-of-staff device that synthesizes context and pushes proactive nudges to keep the user focused on the top three priorities.

nodes.description: A starter personality template used to bootstrap the assistant’s chief-of-staff tone before it evolves from user behavior.
